items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Then along with him, a guy that at that particular time I used to play football with around a lot, whose name was George McIver... So I would sit and play the piano, and he'd sit beside me, and we'd just have a ball in my living room doing these things.

ctx.x: make these little runs up and down the piano. So he and I became fast friends, and we used to sit down and play the piano at my house or his house.

Then along with him, a guy that at that particular time I used to play football with around a lot, whose name was George McIver. And like my mother, and so many people I've met since then that have this I don't know what you'd call it... They have this knack for knowing music, and they never play an instrument, they never studied music or anything, but there's a love that they have for it that just makes them knowledgeable about music beyond a lot of musicians that I've known who studied. In other words, these…

My mother was certainly one of those people, and this fellow George McIver was that kind of a guy. He used to like to tap dance, and he used to like to buy a gift of these horns... We used to call them the kazoo. It's a little thing where you put a piece of paper... There's a little horn, and you put a piece of paper in it (you could do the same thing with a comb) and hum through it and make these sounds.
